items.title: Asset Purchase Facility: Gilt Sales – Market Notice 17 September 2026
items.summary: This Market Notice outlines the Bank Executive’s approach to implementing the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision to unwind the gilts held for monetary policy purposes in the Asset Purchase Facility (APF). As part of this, Bank APF auctions will be paused while the Bank reviews a model of selling gilts to the Government.
items.why: deterministic: corroborated across feeds

items.title: Bank rate maintained at 3.75% - September 2026 Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes
items.summary: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee is responsible for making decisions about Bank Rate.
items.why: deterministic: corroborated across feeds

items.title: Singapore sets national AI missions for financial services
items.summary: Singapore has set itself three national AI missions for financial services, harnessing the technology to strengthen crime prevention, boost access to financing for businesses, and enabling agents to transact safely.
items.why: Singapore announces new national AI policy framework for financial services.

items.title: Cyber resilience guidance consultation and AI and quantum effective practices
items.summary: UK’s financial regulators are proposing a new guidance to help financial services firms prepare for and recover from cyber incidents as threats grow.
items.why: UK regulators propose new cyber resilience guidance covering AI and quantum threats for financial firms.

items.title: Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime
items.summary: The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth.
items.why: UK regulators propose significantly easing Senior Managers and Certification Regime checks to support growth.

items.title: Payoneer scores preliminarily OCC approval for stablecoin bank
items.summary: Cross-border payments firm Payoneer has received preliminary conditional approval from US regulators to form a stablecoin national trust bank.
items.why: Major fintech regulatory milestone: OCC grants conditional approval for stablecoin trust bank.

items.title: 2027-2031 Monetary Policy Framework – Governing Council’s Statement
items.summary: This document sets out the key findings from the latest review. It explains what we learned, what will remain the same and what must continue to evolve as Canada faces a more volatile global economy.
items.why: Official Bank of Canada 2027-2031 monetary policy framework renewal release.

items.title: Worldline shares plummet on FT report on cash advances
items.summary: Shares in Worldline fell by as much as 20% on Friday after the Financial Times reported that the French firm delayed payments to suppliers and asked customers for cash advances ahead of its financial results in the years leading up to a 2023 profit warning.
items.why: Shares plunged 20% following report on delayed supplier payments and cash advances.

items.title: UK SME lender OakNorth secures US banking licence
items.summary: OakNorth, the UK digital bank for SMEs, has secured a US national banking charter, paving the way for it to expand beyond lending in the country.
items.why: UK digital bank secured a US national banking charter for overseas expansion.

items.title: Geordie Shore star sentenced for promoting high-risk investments on social media
items.summary: A UK reality TV star and a 'finfluencer' have been sentenced and fined for illegally promoting an unauthorised foreign exchange trading scheme on social media.
items.why: Court sentencing following regulator prosecution of finfluencer for illegal forex promotion.

items.title: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard say hackers leaked customer emails
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have confirmed that some customer data, including emails, were exposed in cyberattacks on third-party vendors.
items.why: Data breach exposing customer emails across major financial institutions via third-party vendor.

items.title: Adyen co-CEO van der Does retires
items.summary: The co-founder and co-CEO of Dutch payments processor Adyen, Pieter van der Does, is retiring, with his co-chief Ingo Uytdehaage taking sole control.
items.why: Co-founder and co-CEO of major payments processor Adyen is stepping down.

items.title: CFTC loses emergency effort to block New York action against Kalshi
items.summary: A US judge has rejected a request from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to temporarily block the New York Attorney General from pursuing their legal case against prediction market Kalshi.
items.why: US judge rejects CFTC effort to block New York Attorney General action against Kalshi.

items.title: Canada picks FDX for open banking technical standards
items.summary: The Canadian government has chosen US organisation Financial Data Exchange (FDX) as the technical standards body for the country's open banking regime.
items.why: Canadian government selects official technical standards body for national open banking regime.

items.title: JP Morgan, HSBC and StoneX pilot digital gold trades
items.summary: HSBC, JP Morgan and StoneX have carried out the first live trades of fractions of physical gold bars, using it as collateral in legally binding wholesale market transaction.
items.why: First live trade using fractional digital gold as wholesale collateral among major banks.

items.title: As Meta's Muse arrives in the UK, FCA issues agentic AI warning to tech firms
items.summary: On the day that Meta's Muse launched in the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority has warned technology companies and social media platforms that AI agents offering money-related services could face regulatory scrutiny.
items.why: FCA warns tech platforms that agentic AI financial tools face existing regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Nvidia does not intend to reinstate Huang despite calls
items.summary: In his first comments since resigning under pressure over his affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Jensen Huang says he would be honoured to return as Nvidia CEO if the board decides to have him back.
items.why: Major corporate governance decision by Nvidia board refusing former CEO's reinstatement.

items.title: Starling founder Anne Boden sold final stake at cut-price £1.7bn valuation, reports say
items.why: Starling founder sells final stake at a significantly discounted valuation.

items.title: MoonPay joins the race for a trust charter
items.summary: p The crypto firm, whose leading executives include a BNY alum and a former acting chair of the CFTC, applied Tuesday for a banking license with the OCC. /p
items.why: Crypto firm MoonPay formally applies for a national bank charter with OCC.

items.title: Trump vows 'tremendous tax' on companies building data centres abroad
items.summary: US President Donald Trump says he is "not allowing data centres to go into other countries", so that America can win the AI fight against China.
items.why: Proposed tax policy targeting US companies building overseas data centres.

items.title: Hydrogen energy company cuts staff two months after $49m federal grant
items.summary: Two months after receiving a grant to expand into commercial manufacturing, a move expected to create 40 new jobs, Port Kembla company Hysata cuts 17 staff.
items.why: Company cuts jobs just two months after receiving a $49m federal grant intended to create positions.

items.title: UK National Wealth Fund Targets Defence Tech as Budget Capital Flows
items.summary: The NWF is set to back British defence tech firm Uforce days after receiving £15.4bn in fresh Budget capital earmarked partly for the sector. The post UK National Wealth Fund Targets Defence Tech as Budget Capital Flows appeared first on The Fintech Times .
items.why: UK National Wealth Fund executes strategic investment into defence tech following capital injection.

items.title: US court convicts Huawei for deceiving banks about Iran dealings
items.summary: US authorities have long claimed the Chinese tech giant poses national security risks.
items.why: Major criminal conviction against Huawei for bank fraud and deceiving financial institutions.
